This Camper Van Was Built by a Master Welder and It's Reinforced From the Frame Up
21 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy
Lots of skills are transferable to camper van building. The most popular one is woodworking, but there are others, like welding, that can make a difference in how well you can build a home on wheels. That's the case with the van I'd like to discuss today and the man behind the conversion.
What we have here is a project based on an AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created by Cody through his Redmond, Oregon-based company, Untrapped Solutions . I dig the name, it's fitting considering what the company does.
Cody is a master welder and craftsman, having worked as a welder at a ski resort, fabricating rails and boxes without exposed fasteners to help keep riders safe. Moreover, in 2016, he converted his first van and founded Untrapped Solutions in 2020 out of a deep love for the outdoors and travel.
As always, let's first take a look at the exterior. For starters, the van rides on Method wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. Cody further upgraded the van's off-road capabilities by installing an Agile Offroad RIP suspension kit, which comes with front coilovers, rear Fox shocks, and custom-rate rear leaf spring packs.
You can use a ladder on the driver's side to climb on top of the van. There, you'll discover a Roambuilt roof rack that holds a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, a Fiamma F45S awning, and a huge deck platform where you can chill and enjoy the surrounding views. What's more, two cut-outs make space for a Maxxair vent fan and an A/C unit.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy At the rear, you'll come across an Agile Offroad spare tire carrier and an Aluminess PowerLift motorized bike rack. Other notable mods are Roambuilt side steps, and power and water hookups.
The interior is the most distinctive part of the build. Cody does a few things differently in his projects. For instance, all the cabinetry is built around a tubular steel frame that's not fully enclosed in the wood – the frames are the cornerstone of the cabinetry.
This construction makes for a very durable and sturdy setup. Furthermore, Untrapped Solutions takes pride in reinforcing the "bones" of the van itself by installing aluminum reinforcements throughout the van.
You'll notice that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy This van's customer is an architect, and she has an eye for design. She opted for a welcoming, colorful aesthetic – it consists of beige Lonseal Lonridge flooring, a mix of bamboo and blue laminated cabinetry with black framing, walls upholstered in grey woven fabric, and a faux leather ceiling.
The look is complemented by a white solid surface countertop, a bamboo trim for the bathroom door, and pops of color, like an orange panel in the seating area.
Straight ahead of the entrance, Cody devised a bathroom. It has a shower with a handheld sprayer, a white Laveo dry-flush toilet, an L-Track on the back wall for hanging stuff, and a retractable Nautilus door that prevents water from splashing outside the bathroom.
Next, we have the kitchen that's split into two parts, one on each side of the living space. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a pull-out faucet, a single-burner induction stovetop, and an Isotherm fridge with a tiny freezer compartment. On its outer panel that faces the entrance, it has a flip-down table supported by small gas struts.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy Walk just a bit deeper inside the van and you'll reach the dinette area. It comprises two benches facing one another, with a decently sized Lagun table in between.
You can turn the dinette into a small bed, and it's quite simple and quick to do. You must remove the tabletop and use it alongside an extra panel to connect the two benches. Then, rearrange the cushions, and you're good to go. The result is a bed that's 72 inches (182 centimeters) long.
Finally, the rear part of the living space is taken up by a fixed sleeping arrangement measuring 76 inches (193 centimeters) in length and 67 inches (170 centimeters) in width. It offers four overhead cabinets (two on each side), an iPad mount, and two reading lights next to the rear doors. Above, a Nomadic Cooling A/C unit will keep you cool when needed.
The go-to storage spot for gear and bulky items is the garage underneath the bedroom, which is accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the rear doors. It offers abundant storage space in the middle and also has two massive boxes on the sides that accommodate the utility systems.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are an 800 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can top off the batteries by using three sources: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, two under-mounted greywater tanks, and an outdoor shower connection with a mixer. Furthermore, a Rixen's hydronic heating system provides both heated air and hot water.
All in all, every detail in this camper van by Cody and Untrapped Solutions has been carefully thought through – it makes it clear that it was made by a master craftsman.
